title.narrative: Power System Efficiency Improvement Project

description.narrative: The draft power sector master plan 2010, updated 2016, identifies the need to add 11 CCPPs each with 450 MW capacity by 2016. The proposed Ashuganj 450 MW plant (part A) can be considered one of these CCPPs. Further, the government has identified the proposed plant as a priority project in its expansion plan. The economic cost of electricity supply from the Ashuganj CCPP is similar to or lower than those of a coal-fired power plant (based on the costs taken from the master plan), confirming that the proposed plant is among the least-cost options for generating new capacity. CCPP design will use the latest commercially available technology to harness the maximum benefit of energy efficiency. Part B of the project will demonstrate renewable energy technologies and their application for long-term large-scale penetration into the Bangladesh power system. The sub components in part B use solar photovoltaic, wind power and LEDs, which are commercially proven technologies. Additional financing will be utilized for installation of 2,000 solar irrigation pumps in ten different districts of Bangladesh.

Status of Implementation Progress: The project has 3 Outputs:
Part A: 450 MW Ashuganj 450 MW Combined cycle Power plant under APSCL. The plant has been commissioned and operational since 2017.
Part B(i): Kaptai 7.4 MW solar power Plant under BPDB. It has been commissioned and operational since 6 May 2019.
Part B(ii): Original component compising a solar-diesel hybrid power plant in Hatia island was cancelled in 2015. Instead, ADB reallocated the available loan proceeds to BPDB in favor of 1 million smart prepaid meters in April 2021. Implementation is ongoing. Out of 1 million, 0.4 million meters have been installed in BPDB's three distribution area (Cumilla, Sylhet, Chittagong).
Part B(iii): Installation and commissioning of solar street lighting systems in 8 City Corporations by BPDB. Streetlights have been installed and operational in seven city corporations from 30 March 2019.
Part B(iv): 2000 Solar Irrigation Pump by BREB. BREB signed six turnkey contracts for installation and commissioning of the solar pumps in 2020 and 2021. Out of 2000, 608 pumps are installed. A contract to connect 1295 solar pumps with the main grid was signed in Dec 2024 to export the surplus renewable electricity in off-season to main grid.
Part C: Capacity building of the executing and implementing agencies. Implementation support consultants for APSCL and BPDB were recruited within 2016. BREB signed contract with the implementation support consulting firm on 31 January 2019 for design and implementation of 2000 solar irrigation. The implementation support contract is ongoing. For institutional capacity development, BPDB and BREB conducted trainings for their own components. BREB also completed a training program for GAP implementation of 2,000 solar irrigation pumps.
